gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Toybox's own support page says the Toybox takes any third-party 1.75 mm PLA, and that using it 'will not void your warranty'; it rejects any other diameter or material and warns against glitter/speck-filled filament.
standout_why: I compared against printingxyz.com and itechguides.com, which ranked 2 and 3 in the results. printingxyz calls Toybox filament 'proprietary' ('Proprietary filament rolls are expensive', 'Toybox sells its own mini PLA spools'). itechguides only says 'Toybox-compatible PLA filament or the brand's Printer Food refills'. Neither says that third-party PLA is allowed or that the warranty survives it. The cited Tom's Hardware page came back as navigation only ('article body was truncated'), so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answer lists Toybox's catch as 'limited print size and less flexibility', not filament lock-in. Our page says 'filament about $60/kg'. The maker's store today shows $15 per 500 g roll ($30/kg) and $49 for 4×500 g ($24.50/kg), so that cell is wrong.
decides: This keeps the Toybox Alpha Four as the pick for ages 5–8 and removes the 'proprietary refills' cost objection rivals raise. Running costs are standard 1.75 mm PLA from any brand, warranty intact, or Printer Food at $24.50–$37.80/kg. Two limits to state on the page: Wi-Fi is 2.4 GHz only, and the supported devices are iOS, Android or a web browser. Our 'Catch' cell should read 'Outgrown fast; 75 × 80 × 90 mm' instead of '$60/kg filament'.

findings.label: Third-party filament allowed (maker support)
findings.value: Any 1.75 mm PLA; 'will not work with any other size or filament type'; '3rd party filament will not void your warranty'
findings.source_title: Can I use 3rd party filament? – Toybox Labs Help Center
findings.note: Toybox Labs support article. It also says to measure the diameter with calipers if unsure, avoid filament with specks, flecks or glitter because it is 'very prone to clogging', and that Toybox won't recommend specific third-party brands.

findings.label: Filament stated on the product page
findings.value: 'You can import designs from other sites and use other 1.75mm PLA'; Printer Food is what the printer is 'tuned for'
findings.note: The same page says 'Alpha Four uses the same Printer Food rolls as every Toybox'.

findings.label: Wi-Fi band
findings.note: From the spec block 'Wi-Fi: 2.4GHz band'. The page's comparison table was ambiguous for this model.

findings.label: Supported devices / OS
findings.value: iOS, Android or any web browser (print from make.toys)

findings.label: File formats accepted
findings.note: Kids can upload models from other sites or from CAD. Toybox Pro is optional; without it the 25k+ catalog and Creator Space are still available.

findings.label: Price, bundles (maker store)
findings.value: Pro Saver $199 (1 roll + 1 month Pro); Pro Mega $239 (8 rolls + 1 month Pro); Starter $249 (1 roll); Deluxe $299 (8 rolls)
findings.source_title: Toybox Alpha Four Pro Saver 3D Printer Bundle
findings.note: Read from the Toybox Shopify store with storecheck. Each bundle has its own URL: /products/toybox-alpha-four-pro-mega-3d-printer-bundle, /products/toybox-alpha-four-starter-3d-printer-bundle, /products/alpha-four-deluxe-bundle. Strike-through 'compare at' prices are $469, $549, $435 and $489.

findings.label: Printer Food cost per kg (maker store)
findings.note: Single standard roll is $15 per 500 g, so $30/kg (limited/glow rolls are $19, so $38/kg). Mystery bundle (https://toybox.com/products/mystery-printer-food-bundle): $49 ÷ 2 kg = $24.50/kg. Swamp bundle: $65 ÷ 2 kg = $32.50/kg. Deluxe bundle: $60 ÷ (7 × 0.5 lb = 3.5 lb = 1.588 kg) = $37.80/kg. All are 1.75 mm PLA. This contradicts our page's '$60/kg'.

findings.note: Read from the Flashforge Shopify store with storecheck. The refurbished unit is at https://www.flashforge.com/products/flashforge-ad5m-pro-refurbished-3d-printer. The maker copy says 'a child or an adult' and claims filtration of '99% of airborne particulates and VOCs'.

findings.value: BIQU Panda CryoGrip Pro: the maker lists it as made for Bambu Lab X1C, X1E, P1S, P1P, A1 and A1 Mini; PLA at 45–55 °C bed
